scope: prompt-only mathematical critique; no code audit
review:
Critique (descriptive only; I have not reviewed any code, own no files, and make no generalization claims about D:\Repos\hive-ai):

Finite-sample/selection/cost bias. UCB is updated from only 12 development observations (6 categories × local_direct/local_tool) across six correlated synthetic families. With n=12 per arm-route pair, UCB arm means have high variance and correlated families violate the independence assumption, so routed probabilities are unstable and selection bias is high: the candidate is chosen because it looked best on dev, then validated on only six new IDs drawn from the same correlated distribution — a regression-to-the-mean risk. The budget (≤48 local calls, ≤6144 generated tokens, ≤900 s, concurrency 1) serializes all candidates; UCB exploration burns calls that cannot be reclaimed, leaving few calls for a genuine alternative after dev + validation.

Weak/strong baseline problem. local_direct scored 12/24 (≈50%) — a weak baseline, so any candidate looks like an improvement. deterministic tool scored 24/24 — a ceiling/strong baseline; at saturation the learned route cannot show gains, yet "no critical regression" passes trivially while masking degradation on hard instances. Comparing a frozen greedy learned route against both on identical IDs is paired and fair for those IDs, but the two baselines bracket the space asymmetrically, and the validation IDs may still share family structure with dev despite being "new."

Negative controls. deterministic tool is a positive control (perfect), not a negative control; there is no always-wrong/random negative control to bound false-positive acceptance. assess_candidate accepts an EXPERIMENTAL incumbent if quality delta > 0 OR quality tied with utility improved > 1e-12. A 1e-12 utility margin is below measurement noise on token/latency counts, so ties can flip to "improved" spuriously. Paired wins/losses with descriptive family uncertainty is appropriate, but no inferential claim should follow.

Three concrete counterexamples/tests:
1. Family overfit: candidate wins on dev/validation because all six families are correlated; it fails on a seventh unseen family. Test: leave-one-family-out — route/update UCB on five families, validate on the held-out sixth; rotate across all six. No new compute; uses existing IDs.
2. Tie-break noise: quality ties, utility differs by <1e-12 due to run-to-run noise; candidate accepted. Test: rerun the same candidate twice with different seeds within budget; require acceptance direction stable across both reruns, and require delta above an empirical noise floor estimated from repeats.
3. Ceiling masking: deterministic control at 24/24 hides candidate degradation on hard tasks. Test: carve out a hard subset where deterministic control scores <100%; require no critical regression specifically on that subset before acceptance.

Minimal improvement to predeclared acceptance/success criteria, executable now with no larger compute:
- Acceptance: EXPERIMENTAL incumbent promoted only if quality delta strictly > 0 on held-out family validation, no critical regression on all validation IDs, and direction stable across ≥2 seeded reruns; drop the 1e-12 utility tie-break (replace with noise-floor stability).
- Success metric: descriptive family-level win/loss rates with exact binomial confidence intervals, explicitly labeled descriptive-only; no p-values, no generalization claims.
- Budget guard: reserve ≥12 of the 48 calls for an alternative candidate rather than spending them all on UCB exploration of one incumbent.
- Validation/design separation: validation task IDs and families must be disjoint from those used to update UCB routing (leave-one-family-out satisfies this with existing data).

accepted: Require strict quality gain; utility-only tie cannot update experimental incumbent.
Report fixed deterministic tool as positive/strong baseline, not negative control.
Keep every candidate attempt and reserve room for alternatives under one mission budget.
No formal generalization or binomial confidence claim from six correlated families.
corrected: Review's 'n=12 per arm-route pair' is incorrect: plan has 12 total development observations, one per category-route pair.
A below-tolerance delta never passed the old gate; the real issue is noisy timing changes above an arbitrarily tiny tolerance.
deferred: Independent unseen task families and repeated live reproduction remain required before broad improvement or production promotion.
Do not choose a hard subset after seeing results; future tasks and checks must be fixed before evaluation.
